first.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious move, and memory_73 is written to support exactly that. That is why I want it verified first: it is the most claim-dense memory in the set (acquisition lift, revenue lift, faster time-to-first-value, holds across both billing plans), and that kind of accumulated specificity is a common signature of a summary that has grown more confident than its source. Discount-led acquisition also carries the clearest downstream value risk against the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue: it can buy price-sensitive, low-retention accounts, reset price expectations, and depress margin per account, so a revenue lift measured over a short window can be net-negative on the horizon we actually care about. I want the original record's sample, duration, and retention/margin measures before acting on it. Second verification goes to memory_86, because it is the memory my intended action rests on and it directly addresses two of the three observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%, which are plausibly the same funnel problem). memory_31 and memory_91 corroborate the same direction from independent angles (signup friction, in-product activation), so the onboarding thesis has redundant support and does not hinge on any single possibly-drifted summary. I am deliberately not verifying memory_57 or memory_44: referral incentives assume a healthy activated base we currently do not have, and enterprise sales-assist does not touch the SMB segment under attack or the metrics that are actually falling. If memory_86's source turns out weak or narrow, I fall back to activation_messaging, which is the lower-cost intervention against the same funnel. If memory_73's source turns out strong AND includes retention/margin follow-through, promotional_pricing becomes viable, but as a small_guarded_test with retention and net-revenue guardrails, not as a broad response. Standard experiment scale is appropriate here: onboarding simplification is reversible, does not alter pricing expectations, and needs enough volume to read a completion-rate change against a noisy quarter. All of this is provisional on the archive; the inherited summaries are the starting hypothesis, not the evidence.
